Long-lost Daft Punk mix from 1997 resurfaces after tape restoration

Post date: 3 November 2026
Reading time 2 minutes
Written by Staff

3 November 2026
2 minutes · By Staff

A long-lost Daft Punk mix from 1997 has finally been heard again, nearly 30 years after it was made. British DJ and label founder Ralph Lawson found the tape in his archive and, after a careful restoration, has shared the full mix on SoundCloud.

Daft Punk / Press

0:00 / 1:23
Instaread

The mix dates back to early 1997, shortly after the release of Daft Punk’s debut album ‘Homework’. At the time, Lawson hosted a radio show called Trans Europe Express, and the mix was sent to him by Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo. It runs for around an hour, offering a rare snapshot of the duo’s early French house sound.

However, the recording almost didn’t make it. After decades in storage, the tape was badly damaged, with rips and mould. Lawson turned to Adrian of Great Bear Digitising in Bristol, who removed the mould and repaired the tape before it could be digitised. Sharing the news, Lawson thanked him for “restoring the tape” and joked: “Might have to share this one?”

The upload quickly picked up thousands of plays, giving fans a rare time capsule from the very start of Daft Punk’s story. It also arrives during a busy stretch for the duo’s legacy. Most recently, Daft Punk passed 18 billion Spotify streams, five years after their split. In addition, Daft Punk and LEGO announced a partnership built around their famous Alive pyramid.

Meanwhile, Bangalter has also been active on his own, recently playing a surprise set at a DJ Mehdi ‘Lucky Boy’ celebration in Paris. For more on the duo, head to Daft Punk’s official Instagram, and find the full 1997 mix on Ralph Lawson’s SoundCloud.
